questions.prompt: How would you design a URL shortening service like Bitly?
questions.zh: 你会怎么设计一个类似 Bitly 的短链接服务？
outline: Clarify: custom aliases, link expiry, analytics, read-to-write ratio
Estimate: new links per day, redirects per second, storage over five years
Core design: counter plus base62 keys, key-value store, cache in front
Bottlenecks: hot links, key generator as a single point of failure
Trade-offs: 301 versus 302 redirects, real-time analytics versus redirect latency

chunks.zh: 存活时间（缓存过期时间）

followUps: How would you handle a link that suddenly goes viral?
How do you stop people from guessing or scraping short links?

questions.prompt: Design the home timeline for a social network like Twitter.
questions.zh: 设计一个类似 Twitter 的社交网络的首页信息流。
outline: Clarify: follow model, chronological or ranked, media, how fresh the feed must be
Estimate: daily active users, posts per second, average followers per user
Core design: fan-out on write into a cached feed per user
Bottlenecks: celebrity accounts; switch to fan-out on read for them
Trade-offs: freshness versus cost; eventual consistency is acceptable here

chunks.zh: 扇出（一条消息分发给多个下游）

followUps: How would you add ranking without hurting latency?

questions.prompt: Design a real-time chat application like WhatsApp or Slack.
questions.zh: 设计一个类似 WhatsApp 或 Slack 的实时聊天应用。
outline: Clarify: one-to-one or group chat, receipts, history, offline delivery
Estimate: concurrent connections, messages per second, storage per year
Core design: WebSocket gateways, message queue, storage partitioned by conversation
Bottlenecks: stateful connections, very large groups, reconnect storms after an outage
Trade-offs: per-conversation ordering instead of global ordering; deduplicate on the client

chunks.zh: 确认（消息已收到或已处理）
扇出（一条消息分发给多个下游）

followUps: How would you show online presence at this scale?
How would you support end-to-end encryption?

questions.prompt: Design a distributed rate limiter for a public API.
questions.zh: 为一个公开 API 设计一个分布式限流器。
outline: Clarify: limit per user, IP, or API key; hard or soft limits
Estimate: requests per second, number of keys, latency budget per check
Core design: token bucket counters in Redis, enforced at the gateway
Bottlenecks: a counter lookup on every request, races between gateway nodes
Trade-offs: accuracy versus latency; fail open or closed when Redis is down

chunks.zh: 故障时放行（限流器挂了就不拦请求）

followUps: How do you keep the counters accurate across multiple regions?

questions.prompt: Design a notification system that delivers push notifications, emails, and SMS.
questions.zh: 设计一个能发送推送、邮件和短信的通知系统。
outline: Clarify: channels, volume, urgency levels, user preferences, delivery guarantees
Estimate: notifications per day, burst size during campaigns
Core design: one queue per channel, workers calling third-party providers
Bottlenecks: provider rate limits and outages, duplicate sends on retry
Trade-offs: priority lanes for urgent messages, deduplication versus delivery speed

chunks.zh: 消费延迟（消费者落后了多少消息）

followUps: How do you make sure a user never gets the same notification twice?

questions.prompt: Design a flash sale system where limited stock sells out within seconds.
questions.zh: 设计一个秒杀系统，有限的库存会在几秒内卖完。
outline: Clarify: stock size, per-user limit, payment window, fairness requirements
Estimate: peak requests per second compared with items actually available
Core design: reject early at the edge, reserve stock in Redis, queue orders
Bottlenecks: hot inventory key, overselling, bots, the order database
Trade-offs: strict stock accuracy versus throughput; what users see under load
followUps: What happens to reserved stock when a user doesn't pay in time?

questions.prompt: Design the autocomplete suggestions for a search box used by millions of people.
questions.zh: 为一个有几百万人使用的搜索框设计自动补全建议。
outline: Clarify: number of suggestions, personalization, languages, freshness of trending terms
Estimate: one request per keystroke, queries per second, dictionary size
Core design: prefix index with precomputed top results, cached aggressively
Bottlenecks: latency per keystroke, updating popularity without a full rebuild
Trade-offs: freshness versus cost; debounce and cache on the client

chunks.term: good enough for our use case
chunks.zh: 对我们的场景来说已经够用

followUps: How would you filter out offensive suggestions?

questions.prompt: Design a file storage and sync service like Dropbox or Google Drive.
questions.zh: 设计一个类似 Dropbox 或 Google Drive 的文件存储和同步服务。
outline: Clarify: file size limits, sharing, version history, sync across devices
Estimate: total storage, upload bandwidth, metadata operations per second
Core design: chunked uploads to object storage, separate metadata service
Bottlenecks: large uploads on bad networks, sync conflicts, metadata growth
Trade-offs: deduplication versus privacy, last-write-wins versus keeping both copies

chunks.zh: 副本因子（每份数据存几份）
访问模式（数据会怎么被读写）

followUps: Two devices edit the same file offline. What happens when they reconnect?

questions.prompt: Design the payment processing system for an e-commerce platform.
questions.zh: 为一个电商平台设计支付处理系统。
outline: Clarify: payment methods, external providers, refunds, reconciliation, compliance
Estimate: modest transactions per second; correctness matters far more than scale
Core design: payment state machine, idempotent APIs, ledger, provider webhooks
Bottlenecks: provider timeouts, double charges, state drifting between systems
Trade-offs: consistency over availability; synchronous versus asynchronous confirmation
followUps: The provider times out and you don't know whether the charge went through. What do you do?

questions.prompt: Design a distributed job scheduler that can run millions of scheduled tasks a day.
questions.zh: 设计一个每天能运行几百万个定时任务的分布式任务调度系统。
outline: Clarify: one-off or recurring, timing precision, job duration, retry policy
Estimate: jobs per day, how many fall due in the same second
Core design: durable job store, time-bucketed polling, queue, worker pool
Bottlenecks: scheduler failover, duplicate execution, stuck or long-running jobs
Trade-offs: at-least-once execution means jobs must be idempotent
followUps: A worker dies halfway through a job. How does the system find out and recover?

questions.prompt: Design a video streaming platform like YouTube.
questions.zh: 设计一个类似 YouTube 的视频流媒体平台。
outline: Clarify: upload and playback, live or on demand, supported devices
Estimate: uploads per day, storage growth, peak concurrent viewers, bandwidth
Core design: upload service, transcoding pipeline, object storage, CDN delivery
Bottlenecks: transcoding backlog, CDN cost, popular videos, metadata reads
Trade-offs: adaptive bitrate versus storage cost; transcode up front or on demand

questions.prompt: Design a collaborative document editor like Google Docs, where several people edit at once.
questions.zh: 设计一个类似 Google Docs 的协作文档编辑器，多个人可以同时编辑。
outline: Clarify: concurrent editors per document, offline editing, comments, version history
Estimate: active documents, edits per second per document, document size
Core design: WebSocket sessions, operation log, operational transformation or CRDTs
Bottlenecks: conflict resolution, very active documents, growing operation history
Trade-offs: OT needs a central server; CRDTs cost more memory

chunks.zh: 乐观更新（先改界面，再等服务端确认）

followUps: How would you show other people's cursors without flooding the server?

questions.prompt: Design a metrics and alerting platform that monitors thousands of services.
questions.zh: 设计一个监控几千个服务的指标和告警平台。
outline: Clarify: metric types, retention, query patterns, how fast alerts must fire
Estimate: data points per second, number of time series, storage per day
Core design: agents, ingestion queue, time-series store, query and alerting layers
Bottlenecks: label explosion, slow dashboard queries, ingestion spikes during incidents
Trade-offs: downsample old data, sample versus keep everything, alert noise
followUps: How does the monitoring system stay up when everything else is down?

questions.prompt: Design a webhook delivery system that notifies customers' servers when events happen.
questions.zh: 设计一个 webhook 投递系统，在事件发生时通知客户的服务器。
outline: Clarify: delivery guarantee, ordering, payload size, retry window, security
Estimate: events per second, number of endpoints, share of slow or failing ones
Core design: persist events, queue per endpoint, workers sending signed requests
Bottlenecks: one slow customer blocking others, retry floods after an outage
Trade-offs: at-least-once means customers must deduplicate; ordering is best effort

chunks.zh: 加随机抖动（让重试时间错开）

followUps: How can a customer verify that a webhook really came from you?

questions.prompt: Your company's monolith is slowing teams down. How would you break it up into services?
questions.zh: 公司的单体应用拖慢了各个团队。你会怎么把它拆成服务？
outline: Clarify: what hurts today: deploys, scaling, or team ownership
Scale: number of teams, release frequency, how coupled the data is
Core approach: find service boundaries, extract one piece at a time
Bottlenecks: shared database, distributed transactions, more operational overhead
Trade-offs: a well-structured monolith may be enough; say so

chunks.zh: 绞杀者模式（逐步替换旧系统）
不值得为此增加复杂度

followUps: Which piece would you extract first, and why?

questions.prompt: A service is struggling under read load. How would you add a caching layer to it?
questions.zh: 一个服务在读压力下撑不住了。你会怎么给它加一层缓存？
outline: Clarify: which queries are slow, how stale the data may be
Scale: read-to-write ratio, hot keys, data size, current latency
Core design: cache-aside with a TTL, invalidate on write
Bottlenecks: stampede on hot keys, cold cache after a deploy, memory limits
Trade-offs: staleness versus load; maybe fix the slow queries first

chunks.zh: 缓存失效（主动让缓存作废）
缓存击穿（热点键过期，大量请求同时回源）

followUps: The database write succeeds but the cache invalidation fails. What then?

questions.prompt: How would you migrate a large production database to a new schema or datastore with zero downtime?
questions.zh: 你会怎么在不停机的情况下，把一个很大的生产数据库迁移到新的表结构或新的存储上？
outline: Clarify: data size, write rate, acceptable risk, rollback requirements
Estimate: how long the backfill takes and the extra load it adds
Core design: dual writes, backfill, verify, switch reads, then switch writes
Bottlenecks: keeping both sides consistent, long backfills, replication lag
Trade-offs: a slow phased cutover versus a risky big-bang switch
followUps: How do you verify that the old and new stores hold the same data?

questions.prompt: Your primary database has become the bottleneck. What options do you have, and in what order would you try them?
questions.zh: 主数据库成了瓶颈。你有哪些办法？会按什么顺序去尝试？
outline: Clarify: read or write bottleneck, slow queries or raw volume
Scale: query patterns, table sizes, growth rate, connection usage
Core path: indexes and query fixes, caching, read replicas, then sharding
Bottlenecks: replication lag on replicas, cross-shard queries, resharding later
Trade-offs: each step adds operational complexity; exhaust the cheap options first
followUps: How would you choose the shard key?

questions.prompt: A critical service depends on several unreliable downstream services. How would you keep it available?
questions.zh: 一个关键服务依赖好几个不稳定的下游服务。你会怎么保证它的可用性？
outline: Clarify: which dependencies are critical and which are optional
Scale: failure rates, latency distribution, what the SLO requires
Core design: timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers, fallbacks, isolation
Bottlenecks: retries amplifying load, thread pools exhausted by slow calls
Trade-offs: serving degraded or stale data versus returning errors
followUps: How would you test that these protections actually work?

questions.prompt: How would you take a system that runs in a single region and make it multi-region?
questions.zh: 一个只部署在单个区域的系统，你会怎么把它做成多区域部署？
outline: Clarify: the goal: lower latency, disaster recovery, or data residency
Estimate: traffic per region, data volume, tolerable data loss and downtime
Core design: active-passive first, replicate data, route traffic by region
Bottlenecks: cross-region replication lag, write conflicts, failover that was never tested
Trade-offs: active-active cuts latency but forces you to handle conflicts
followUps: How often would you rehearse a regional failover, and how?

questions.prompt: You need to make a breaking change to a public API that many clients depend on. How do you design and roll it out?
questions.zh: 你要对一个很多客户端都在用的公开 API 做不兼容的改动。你会怎么设计、怎么上线？
outline: Clarify: who the clients are and how fast they can upgrade
Scale: usage per endpoint and per client version
Core design: new version alongside the old, compatibility layer, migration guide
Bottlenecks: clients that never upgrade, maintaining two code paths
Trade-offs: deprecation timeline versus customer pain; commit to a sunset date

chunks.zh: 弃用（标记为不推荐使用）

followUps: What do you do about a large customer who refuses to migrate?

questions.prompt: Users complain that a key dashboard page takes ten seconds to load. How would you investigate and fix it?
questions.zh: 用户抱怨一个重要的仪表盘页面要十秒才能加载出来。你会怎么排查和解决？
outline: Clarify: slow for everyone or only some users, and since when
Scale: data volume behind the page, number of requests it makes
Core approach: measure each layer first, then parallelize, precompute, cache
Bottlenecks: chatty APIs, heavy aggregation queries, oversized bundles
Trade-offs: precomputed data is fast but stale; agree on a target

chunks.zh: 请求瀑布（请求一个等一个，串行发出）

followUps: How would you make sure it doesn't quietly get slow again?

questions.prompt: Design the backend for a multi-tenant SaaS product. How do you isolate tenants' data and performance?
questions.zh: 为一个多租户 SaaS 产品设计后端。你怎么隔离各个租户的数据和性能？
outline: Clarify: number of tenants, size skew, compliance and isolation requirements
Estimate: data per tenant, the largest tenant compared with the median
Core design: shared schema with a tenant ID, or a database per tenant
Bottlenecks: noisy neighbors, one huge tenant, migrations across many databases
Trade-offs: isolation versus cost and operational effort; hybrid for big customers

chunks.zh: 吵闹的邻居（某个租户占用过多资源，拖累其他租户）

followUps: How do you guarantee one tenant can never read another tenant's data?

questions.prompt: Design authentication and authorization for a product with web and mobile clients and multiple backend services.
questions.zh: 为一个有 Web 端、移动端和多个后端服务的产品设计认证和授权。
outline: Clarify: login methods, single sign-on, session length, permission model
Estimate: logins and token validations per second, number of services
Core design: central identity service, short-lived access tokens, refresh tokens
Bottlenecks: token validation on every request, revoking tokens quickly
Trade-offs: stateless tokens versus server-side sessions, convenience versus security
followUps: A user's token is stolen. How quickly can you cut off access, and how?

questions.prompt: An order flow spans the order, inventory, and payment services. How do you keep the data consistent when one step fails?
questions.zh: 一个下单流程跨了订单、库存和支付三个服务。其中一步失败时，你怎么保证数据一致？
outline: Clarify: which steps must be atomic, how long inconsistency is tolerable
Estimate: order volume, failure rate of each step, peak load
Core design: saga with compensating steps, events published through an outbox
Bottlenecks: partial failures, duplicate or out-of-order events, stuck sagas
Trade-offs: eventual consistency versus the coupling and latency of two-phase commit

chunks.zh: 把长事务拆成多个本地事务、失败就逐步补偿的模式

followUps: Would you use orchestration or choreography for the saga, and why?
